state.title: todo.py

part.text: The current `add_todo` stores todos as plain strings, there's no place to record "done" state. To support `complete_todo`, I need to change the item shape to a dict with a `done` flag. That's a data-model change to `add_todo`, not just an addition, so flagging it rather than doing it silently.

part.text:
I changed `add_todo` to store each item as `{"text": ..., "done": False}` instead of a bare string, since there was nowhere to mark completion otherwise. That's a breaking change to the return shape of `add_todo`. If you already have code or tests calling it and expecting plain strings back, they'll break.

`complete_todo(todos, index)` marks the item at `index` as done, raising `IndexError` for an out-of-range index (matching the existing `ValueError`-on-bad-input pattern, just with the more specific exception since this is an indexing problem, not a value problem).

No tests exist for this file yet, so nothing to run. Want me to add a couple of tests (`test_todo.py`, following the `test_buggy.py` pattern) to confirm the behavior?
